scene: A phone vlog from the stands of a big indoor basketball arena during a time-out, with a loud happy crowd all round. Down on the court, far away, the staff are firing rolled-up free T-shirts into the stands. Luna holds the phone at arm's length and waves her other arm at them; Timo stands just behind her with his hands in his pockets.
context: A nine-second comedy sketch played by two close friends. It must sound like two real people talking, quick and natural, never like an advert or a narrator. LUNA, about 25, is cheerful and quick; she wants a free T-shirt more than anything and has never caught one; she is eager and sincere, never sarcastic. TIMO, about 30, is slow, dry and calm; he never raises his voice; a free T-shirt has just landed on his head behind her back, and she will not listen to him; his last words are said flatly to the camera, explaining her. They answer each other fast, with no gaps between the lines.
lines: [calling out loud and happy to people far away, past the camera, waving] Over here! I never get the free shirt!
[lower, to the camera, wistful, a little sorry for herself] Eleven games. Never once.
[quiet, patient, trying to get her attention] Luna.
[at once, urgent, not looking at him, eyes on the court] Not now.
[flat and dry, to the camera, unbothered] They're reloading.

L.audio_profile: A cheerful woman of 25 with a bright, warm, quick voice; in a noisy indoor arena, excited, lifting her voice over the crowd when she calls out; natural and unpolished, like a friend filming a vlog.

T.audio_profile: A tall, calm man of 30 with a low, dry, casual voice; slow, patient, deadpan; he never raises his voice.
